Kansas Jayhawks.status: New starter, identity undetermined — Jalon Daniels is gone and the guide names no successor.
Kansas Jayhawks.competition: Not resolved and not itemised. The guide states only that the quarterback situation looks ugly with Daniels — one of the best dual threats in the sport last year — gone, and refers to Kansas' “quarterback options” without naming them.
Kansas Jayhawks.author_confidence: Low, and expressed as a stated deficiency rather than an assessment of any player. The guide says the quarterback situation looks ugly.
Kansas Jayhawks.positive_case: Not addressed in guide for any quarterback; the guide's positive case is the return of coordinator Andy Kotelnicki, meaning Kansas will run the most successful offense it has used in decades.
Kansas Jayhawks.concerns: The loss of Jalon Daniels' playmaking, which the guide says had masked deficiencies, plus a receiver room that appears to lack game-changing talent.
Kansas Jayhawks.scheme_fit: Kotelnicki's pro-style system uses heavy pre-snap motion to create mismatches, but the guide stresses none of it works without an efficient, physical run game — making line play critical, especially with quarterback uncertainty.
Kansas Jayhawks.supporting_cast: Line promising, receivers not. Kansas is set at left tackle with Calvin Clements, who started 12 games and looks like a future pro, has left guard Amir Herring back, and added impressive bodies elsewhere, with the guide seeing real potential for one of the better Big 12 lines. The receiver room appears to lack game-changing talent.
Kansas Jayhawks.portal_context: Not addressed in guide at quarterback.
Kansas Jayhawks.betting_implications: Recommendation is Under 5.5 wins. Without Daniels' playmaking to mask deficiencies the guide expects a tough year, and says this is not a team to trust in 50-50 games given the quarterback options and a mediocre defense. It closes by noting that if things go extremely poorly, Leipold's situation becomes interesting.
Kansas Jayhawks.outlook_dependency: Very high. The quarterback options are named as one of the two reasons not to trust Kansas in close games.
Kansas Jayhawks.conflicts: The guide declines to name a starter or list the candidates, so this record carries no VSiN preseason expectation for the position.

Kansas State Wildcats.career_experience: Two seasons as starter, which the guide compares directly.
Kansas State Wildcats.previous_starts: Not addressed in guide as a start count.
Kansas State Wildcats.passing: 2,712 yards with 25 touchdowns and 10 interceptions in 2024; 2,385 yards, 18 touchdowns and six interceptions in 2025.
Kansas State Wildcats.rushing: 605 rushing yards and seven scores in 2024; 477 rushing yards and eight scores in 2025.
Kansas State Wildcats.efficiency: Not addressed in guide as a completion rate; the guide's measure is the year-over-year comparison, which shows no improvement.
Kansas State Wildcats.competition: None described — Johnson is the settled starter.
Kansas State Wildcats.author_confidence: Openly questioning, then constructive. The guide asks directly whether this is simply who he is, then argues there should be another gear.
Kansas State Wildcats.positive_case: Among the nation's most impressive athletes at the position, an electric dual threat, with Klein's return meaning what the guide calls a perfect scheme fit.
Kansas State Wildcats.concerns: He did not improve in 2025 on his 2024 production, and the guide says he must earn back lost trust.
Kansas State Wildcats.scheme_fit: Called a perfect fit — Matt Klein's return should suit him — though the guide adds separately that it is not sold on Klein instantly fixing the offense.
Kansas State Wildcats.supporting_cast: Weakened at receiver. Jayce Brown caught 41 balls for 712 yards and five touchdowns as a genuine deep threat and his big-play ability drew Lane Kiffin, so he is now at LSU. Jaron Tibbs and Josh Manning have been productive before, but the guide asks whether either can consistently create space when Klein is not scheming them open, and offers Izaiah Williams, who followed Klein from Texas A&M, as a possible breakout. It calls the receiver group mediocre.
Kansas State Wildcats.portal_context: Jayce Brown left for LSU; Izaiah Williams followed Klein from Texas A&M.
Kansas State Wildcats.betting_implications: Recommendation is Under 7.5 wins. The guide acknowledges why people like the Wildcats as sneaky-good while judging seven wins likelier than eight, and lists its doubts: home games are the tougher ones, Kansas State can easily be tripped up by Houston, Kansas and Arizona in Manhattan, questions stopping the run remain, it is not sold on Klein instantly fixing the offense, Johnson must earn back lost trust, and the receiver group is mediocre.
Kansas State Wildcats.outlook_dependency: Very high. The guide ties the win total explicitly to the quarterback — eight or nine wins requires him sharper as a passer while keeping his running threat.

Oklahoma State Cowboys.status: Transfer — arriving with head coach Eric Morris from North Texas.
Oklahoma State Cowboys.career_experience: The guide calls him the best Group of Five quarterback in the country, with the best numbers of any FBS quarterback.
Oklahoma State Cowboys.previous_starts: Not addressed in guide as a start count.
Oklahoma State Cowboys.passing: Not quantified on Oklahoma State's pages; the guide states he posted the best numbers of any FBS quarterback.
Oklahoma State Cowboys.rushing: Not addressed in guide as production; the guide credits his mobility.
Oklahoma State Cowboys.efficiency: Not addressed in guide as a rate; NFL scouts are drawn to his arm, mobility and ability to read defenses.
Oklahoma State Cowboys.turnovers: More interceptions than touchdowns in two of North Texas's biggest games, against South Florida and at Tulane — the guide's specific counter-evidence.
Oklahoma State Cowboys.competition: None described — Mestemaker is presented as the starter.
Oklahoma State Cowboys.author_confidence: High on production, explicit about the translation question. The guide calls him a legitimate offensive star while insisting he must prove he can handle tougher competition.
Oklahoma State Cowboys.positive_case: The best Group of Five quarterback in the country with the best numbers of any FBS quarterback, and NFL scouts drawn to his arm, mobility and ability to read defenses.
Oklahoma State Cowboys.concerns: Whether it translates to Power Four competition — with the guide fair in noting the two bad games were not only on him — and an offensive line whose quality is genuinely open.
Oklahoma State Cowboys.scheme_fit: Continuity — Morris is another Air Raid coach who brought a group of his former players for year one, Mestemaker among them.
Oklahoma State Cowboys.supporting_cast: Uncertain up front. Oklahoma State lost seven players from last year's offensive line options, so Morris added second-team All-AAC guard Johnny Dickson, three Power Four starters and a starting guard from Coastal Carolina. The guide notes experience will not be lacking but leaves quality genuinely open, framing this as one of the most important position groups in the country this year.
Oklahoma State Cowboys.portal_context: Morris brought a group of his former North Texas players including Mestemaker, and rebuilt the offensive line through the portal.
Oklahoma State Cowboys.betting_implications: Recommendation is Over 5.5 wins. The path is arithmetic: easy wins over Tulsa and Murray State, winnable home games against UCF, Colorado and Kansas, then just one road win needed from West Virginia, Iowa State and Kansas State. The guide identifies the 12 September game against Oregon as Mestemaker's early test, and calls the defense potentially one of the Big 12's worst — which is why it is hard to fully buy Oklahoma State as a conference sleeper.
Oklahoma State Cowboys.outlook_dependency: Very high. The guide's model is explicitly that the defense only needs to be good enough to let Mestemaker win games, as at North Texas.

TCU Horned Frogs.status: Transfer — from Harvard, replacing Josh Hoover, who transferred to Indiana.
TCU Horned Frogs.rushing: Not addressed in guide as production; the guide describes him as more mobile than Hoover.
TCU Horned Frogs.turnovers: Not addressed in guide as a count; the guide characterizes him as less mistake-prone than Hoover.
TCU Horned Frogs.competition: None described — Craig is presented as the starter.
TCU Horned Frogs.author_confidence: Moderate and specific. The guide expects Craig to be productive — less aggressive than Hoover, but less mistake-prone and more mobile.
TCU Horned Frogs.positive_case: Less mistake-prone and more mobile than his predecessor, with a clear role: distributing to playmakers, of which TCU has plenty including talented receiver Jordan Dwyer.
TCU Horned Frogs.concerns: He replaces genuine production — Hoover threw for 3,949 yards with 27 touchdowns and 11 interceptions in 2024 and 3,472 yards with 29 touchdowns and 13 interceptions last year — and the guide names an offensive overhaul that feels a bit ambitious among its three reasons for the Under.
TCU Horned Frogs.scheme_fit: A real stylistic break. New coordinator Gordon Sammis arrives from UConn, whose offense ranked sixth nationally in EPA per play at 0.13 per Game on Paper. TCU normally runs the Air Raid and Sammis runs a pro-style offense, so the guide says this may look nothing like a standard Dykes team — and argues the timing could be ideal precisely because Hoover has gone.
TCU Horned Frogs.supporting_cast: Strong. TCU will lean on a massive offensive line and a good running back group — still throwing, but as a more physical team — with plenty of playmakers including Jordan Dwyer.
TCU Horned Frogs.portal_context: Craig in from Harvard; Hoover out to Indiana.
TCU Horned Frogs.betting_implications: Recommendation is Under 7.5 wins, citing tricky schedule spots and defensive holes. The guide explicitly notes the prevailing sentiment — that people covering the team make TCU live for double-digit wins — before setting out why it disagrees, naming a tough schedule, an offensive overhaul that feels a bit ambitious, and uncertainty at linebacker.
TCU Horned Frogs.outlook_dependency: Moderate. The quarterback change is folded into the wider offensive overhaul the guide doubts, but its sharpest stated risk is linebacker play.

Texas Tech Red Raiders.status: New starter — promoted after Brendan Sorsby, one of the portal's biggest prizes, was ruled ineligible.
Texas Tech Red Raiders.career_experience: A four-star recruit with solid moments in relief; the guide notes Texas Tech was not planning to start him.
Texas Tech Red Raiders.previous_starts: Not addressed in guide as a start count.
Texas Tech Red Raiders.passing: Cited game: a road performance at Utah with 169 passing yards, two touchdowns and no interceptions in a blowout win.
Texas Tech Red Raiders.rushing: 61 rushing yards in that same game at Utah.
Texas Tech Red Raiders.efficiency: Not addressed in guide as a rate; the guide calls him reasonably accurate.
Texas Tech Red Raiders.turnovers: No interceptions in the cited game.
Texas Tech Red Raiders.competition: None described as live — but the situation exists only because Sorsby is ineligible.
Texas Tech Red Raiders.author_confidence: Explicitly uncertain. The guide weighs both sides and concludes there is uncertainty at the most important position.
Texas Tech Red Raiders.positive_case: A four-star recruit who is athletic and reasonably accurate, with solid moments already on the road at Utah.
Texas Tech Red Raiders.concerns: Inexperience, a torn ACL to come back from, and a staff that probably wanted him on the bench another year or two — while handing him the keys to a championship-caliber team.
Texas Tech Red Raiders.supporting_cast: Strong overall but thinner up front. Fifteen players who started in 2025 return. Texas Tech lost two offensive line starters including second-team All-Big 12 guard Davion Carter and could not bring in clear replacements, so it will rely on part-time starters who transferred in or younger players — and the guide sets two requirements: the line must be excellent for Hammond to play well, and it must open holes for star running back Cameron Dickey.
Texas Tech Red Raiders.portal_context: The guide describes McGuire as fishing with dynamite in the portal, with as deep a funding pool as any programme. It records that Brendan Sorsby, one of the portal's biggest prizes, is ineligible this year after being caught betting on sports earlier in his career.
Texas Tech Red Raiders.betting_implications: Recommendation is Over 10.5 wins. The guide concedes selling 11 wins at nearly -200 is a tough ask while judging the number pretty likely: even without an elite quarterback the roster is loaded and the schedule is extremely weak. It says not to be surprised if Texas Tech cruises to the playoff, and names the two things that could burn them — disappointing quarterback play and the slightest defensive dip.
Texas Tech Red Raiders.outlook_dependency: Very high as a risk, low as a requirement. The guide argues the Over holds even without an elite quarterback, while naming disappointing quarterback play as one of only two things that could derail the season.

UCF Golden Knights.career_experience: Started for a good James Madison team; the guide describes him as a leader and proven winner.
UCF Golden Knights.previous_starts: Not addressed in guide as a start count.
UCF Golden Knights.passing: 2,806 yards with 23 touchdowns and eight interceptions at James Madison.
UCF Golden Knights.efficiency: Not addressed in guide as a completion rate; the guide calls him a high-level dual threat.
UCF Golden Knights.competition: None described — Barnett is presented as the starter.
UCF Golden Knights.author_confidence: High, and stated as a change in kind: the guide says the quarterback position goes from a mess to a strength.
UCF Golden Knights.positive_case: A high-level dual threat with strong James Madison production, described as a leader and proven winner, joining plentiful skill-position talent.
UCF Golden Knights.concerns: Not addressed as a quarterback concern; the guide's condition for the offense is the offensive line.
UCF Golden Knights.supporting_cast: Improving but unproven up front. UCF lost four of five offensive line starters, which the guide reframes as opportunity since this was one of the Big 12's worst lines: Preston Cushman is the lone returnee and was at Ole Miss two years ago, two more full-time starters arrived plus another who played a good number of games, and Connor Meadows returns after starting several games at center. Its calibrated conclusion is not one of the better Big 12 lines, but improvement. Skill talent is plentiful, with Duane Thomas and Dylan Wade the more dangerous receiving weapons and Josh Derry intriguing after lighting up the FCS at Monmouth.
UCF Golden Knights.portal_context: Barnett arrives from James Madison as part of portal work the guide says is moving in the right direction; UCF has 13 returning starters against 10 last season, with key spots upgraded.
UCF Golden Knights.betting_implications: Recommendation is Over 5.5 wins, with UCF expected to be bowl bound. The guide maps expected wins over Bethune-Cookman, Georgia State and Iowa State, then seven winnable games from which UCF needs only three — which it calls extremely reasonable given the roster.
UCF Golden Knights.outlook_dependency: High. The guide's case for a significant offensive leap runs through the quarterback upgrade, conditional on the line.

Utah Utes.status: Returning starter — but the guide records that Utah will also give Byrd Ficklin snaps.
Utah Utes.career_experience: First Utah season completed; the guide notes minor accuracy gains in it.
Utah Utes.previous_starts: Not addressed in guide as a start count.
Utah Utes.passing: 2,490 yards with 24 touchdowns and only five interceptions.
Utah Utes.efficiency: Not addressed in guide as a completion rate; the guide records minor accuracy gains in his first Utah season.
Utah Utes.turnovers: Only five interceptions against 24 touchdown passes.
Utah Utes.competition: Not a formal competition, but the guide states the team will give Byrd Ficklin snaps and is candid about the risk, invoking the adage that two quarterbacks means none.
Utah Utes.backup: Byrd Ficklin, who the guide says will get snaps.
Utah Utes.author_confidence: Mixed. The guide credits a dynamic dual threat with strong ratios while naming his arm abandoning him in big games as one of its three reasons for the Under.
Utah Utes.positive_case: A dynamic dual threat with 24 touchdowns to five interceptions plus 835 rushing yards, showing minor accuracy gains.
Utah Utes.concerns: His arm abandoning him in big games last year; the two-quarterback plan; and what happens against elite defenses, with the guide asking whether Utah can convert consistently on third and long.
Utah Utes.scheme_fit: Complicated by a coordinator departure — Jason Beck left for Michigan with Whittingham.
Utah Utes.supporting_cast: The guide's clearest weakness. Utah normally has big linemen and blocking is rarely a problem, but the Utes return no starters at all, with Montana State transfer Cedric Jefferson the only projected starter who consistently started games in 2025. There are impressive young pieces including true freshman Kelvin Obot. Its judgement is unambiguous: nothing suggests one of the better Big 12 units, and the offense will not look good without strong blocking.
Utah Utes.portal_context: Cedric Jefferson arrives from Montana State; Whittingham took coordinator Jason Beck and defensive stars John Henry Daley and Smith Snowden with him to Michigan.
Utah Utes.betting_implications: Recommendation is Under 8.5 wins. The guide grants both the difficulty of winning at Rice-Eccles Stadium and Utah's impressive top-end talent, then states its three reasons together: the loss of a legendary coach, a team weaker in the trenches than usual, and Dampier's arm abandoning him in big games. It identifies the 12 September Arkansas game as an early indicator.
Utah Utes.outlook_dependency: Very high. Big-game quarterback play is one of the three named pillars of the Under.

West Virginia Mountaineers.previous_school: Oklahoma — the guide notes he made big plays there.
West Virginia Mountaineers.career_experience: Made big plays at Oklahoma before West Virginia.
West Virginia Mountaineers.previous_starts: Not addressed in guide as a start count.
West Virginia Mountaineers.passing: Not quantified; the guide describes him as underwhelming as a passer with clear room to improve as a thrower.
West Virginia Mountaineers.rushing: Not quantified; the guide calls him a good runner and an electric runner.
West Virginia Mountaineers.competition: None described — Hawkins is the settled starter.
West Virginia Mountaineers.author_confidence: Split by skill and stated as one of two reasons for the Under: a good runner but underwhelming as a passer.
West Virginia Mountaineers.positive_case: An electric runner who made big plays at Oklahoma and should suit the Rodriguez offense.
West Virginia Mountaineers.concerns: Passing. The guide names him underwhelming as a thrower with clear room to improve, and says the offense would have to be flat-out special to carry the defense — which it doubts.
West Virginia Mountaineers.scheme_fit: Explicitly good — the guide says Hawkins should suit the Rodriguez offense.
West Virginia Mountaineers.supporting_cast: Improving in the run game, weak at receiver. Cam Cook arrives from Jacksonville State after 1,659 rushing yards and 16 touchdowns and should be among the conference's best backs, giving West Virginia a running element it lacked, helped by an improved line. Receiver is the one group the guide says disappoints, with no clarity on who makes plays on money downs and Jaden Bray the best guess.
West Virginia Mountaineers.portal_context: West Virginia added big-time transfer talent on offense including Cam Cook from Jacksonville State.
West Virginia Mountaineers.betting_implications: Recommendation is Under 5.5 wins. The guide expects a 2-0 start against Coastal Carolina and Tennessee-Martin before a tough Virginia game and then Oklahoma State at home to open Big 12 play — a result it says could decide the Over or Under. Its lean rests on two specifics: Hawkins is a good runner but underwhelming as a passer, and the defense needs to be much better after being torched.
West Virginia Mountaineers.outlook_dependency: Very high. Hawkins' passing is one of the two named reasons for the Under.
